latestAccuracySteering.additionalServicePriority: Because actual100-column3%-target sampling exhausted the1s service budget in all6 no-small-index arms, include a minimal bounded100-column TDE under-load comparison at relaxed10% (plus matched control and existing3% evidence). Test whether reduced draws actually improve budget/precision outcomes, rather than infer from static checkpoints.5% can be static if a full service factorial would add little. Split scripts within20min limits; avoid an exhaustive redundant factorial.
latestAccuracySteering.conditionMechanisms: Distinguish effects on statistical accuracy, cost under a fixed budget, and freshness. Key-space sparsity/cell-density variance affect sampling interval convergence; page-level row-size/density heterogeneity, stats sample pages and staleness affect metadata error. A small index, cache, TDE, row width and MVCC mainly change read/CPU/time cost and therefore attainable precision within a fixed budget; they do not make a completed snapshotCOUNT approximate. Concurrent writes/replica lag can change the represented time/population and must not be conflated with estimator error. More sample pages/ANALYZE does not guarantee monotonic accuracy and has separate maintenance impact.
latestAccuracySteering.implementation: Root added isolated bench/accuracy_frontier.py plus01c-ACCURACY-COST and01d-ACCURACY-SERVICE-100 (.versions8.4.13/.encrypted/.outputs). No active imported source was edited. Code is prepared, NOT DB-executed. Review/fix these scripts rather than duplicate.01c uses seven fixtures xfive seeds x3targets, fullCOUNT paired comparisons, target-specific predeclared looks and same alpha.01d uses100-column TDE with control/exact/3%/10%, index absent/present, indexed/nonindexed writes x3repeats=48arms.5% service is explicitly unmeasured; static includes it. Pure arithmetic verifies each first look can meet its target at zero variance; static closure includes new module and sampling dependencies. Both new wrappers honor the review-only aggregate guard (exit3, never success) and declare their required .outputs. Final all has no aggregate cap.
latestAccuracySteering.interpretation: Compare accuracy, elapsed time, read volume and service impact rather than require only3%. Include exactCOUNT at0% error. Choose the most favorable method within the accepted error, freshness and service budget;10% is not an unconditional guarantee for arbitrary unknown tables.
latestAccuracySteering.newExperiment: Review and run the isolated implementation named in implementation after the current owner ends. Retain hypotheses and proper confidence/look allocation. Repair demonstrated issues or split if20min is insufficient; do not duplicate experiments or infer unobserved service effects.
latestAccuracySteering.reporting: Give a compact condition-by-method comparison with accuracy/freshness/cost/limitations and recommended paths. Distinguish interval target from realized error and from global confidence. Relaxed accuracy does not prove no service impact.

Integrated the third lab run. Data intact; 18 of 19 scripts succeeded. Main change: FORCE INDEX (PRIMARY) moved from rejected to conditional, because under scattered writes the secondary-index statement hit its 120 s limit in 4/4 runs while PRIMARY finished 8/8. Under writes that do not touch the index, the earlier result stands. Also: the default parallelism is kept for PK-only tables, a client timeout does not stop the server statement, the ENUM guard, replica STOP failure and channel gate are measured, type results now cover all 5 versions, and the catalog is re-based on the re-run of script 10. New low finding: the step ceiling stops shrunken walks early. Reviewers decide closure.

Rejected. The write-mix redesign is good, its numbers match, and FIND-O6-WRITE-SHAPE-01 closes. Two middle items replace it. FIND-O10-PRIMARY-SCALE answers the author's question: no, adopting FORCE PRIMARY is not shown beyond a 2 GB table near lab saturation, and at 100 writes/s the fixed tolerance is not met against k. FIND-O10-INDEXED-100-STALL: an unexplained 66.8 s split and a whole-run write p95 of 1646.57 ms at 100 writes/s are missing from the text. On 91: encrypted results now exist from a run outside this workflow, so §11 is stale; I would not make them decisive, since encrypted tables are out of scope, but the owner should decide and confirm that run is finished. Scripts 90, 91 and 92 are still of unknown origin to me.
